drhp.business: ECK, the Engineering Division of the Company, makes calender machines and calender rolls - high-precision components that require material expertise, precision machining and balancing technology - as part of the broader machinery / capital goods industry that supplies production equipment to manufacturing sectors. Its end users are textile mills, paper and packaging plants, plastic film manufacturers and the sheet metal industry, served in both domestic and international markets. risks.note: Demand for the Company's products was affected mainly due to a slowdown in the global textile industry; opportunities for calender machines and rolls depend upon growth of textiles, paper, packaging and technical textiles, so the order profile tracks its customers' capex cycle rather than its own.
risks.risk: End-market dependence on the textile cycle

risks.note: The present geopolitical situation has led to demand and supply chain disruption worldwide, which has affected the Company's sales to Bangladesh and other countries and has negatively affected performance.
risks.risk: Geopolitical tension and supply-chain disruption hitting exports

risks.note: Management states that due to the niche nature of the Company's products it is challenging to grow revenue at a fast pace while still maintaining good profit margins; the stated answer is to grow the higher-value calender machine business.
risks.risk: Niche product line caps growth without sacrificing margin

risks.note: Manpower development is named as a primary risk in the risk management policy, and MD&A states the Company has found it challenging to recruit suitable talent for its engineering business - acute for a business whose moat is precision machining and balancing expertise.
